article_title: Can smoking cessation be taught online? A prospective study comparing e-learning and role-playing in medical education.
citation: Lauerer Elias, Tiedemann Elena, Polak Thomas, Simmenroth Anne. (2021). Can smoking cessation be taught online? A prospective study comparing e-learning and role-playing in medical education. International Journal of Medical Education, 12, 12-21. https://doi.org/10.5116/ijme.5ff9.bccc
title: 90-minute 5A smoking cessation counselling training module with parallel online and role-playing variants
description: A newly designed one-time 90-minute course implemented in the compulsory module on prevention and health promotion, teaching the 5A's (ask, advise, assess, assist, arrange) brief intervention model. Structure and content were identical across variants, using the same graphics and explanations; the seminar variant used small role-play groups of three students with rotating doctor, patient and observer roles and structured feedback, while the online variant used a 14-minute video with a commenting background voice and Prezi mind-map presentation. All students received a pocket card summarising the 5A's model and the Fagerström test.
requirements: Three instructors available for questions and feedback in the seminar variant
Email support to solve technical problems with the online module
constraints: Both interventions were designed as a one-time 90-minute course with identical structure and content
The video example was in English while the role-play and OSCE were in German
target_learning_goals: smoking cessation counselling skills following the 5A's model
knowledge of nicotine dependence and therapy options
examples: At the University of Würzburg, 145 third-year students were randomly allocated to the seminar or online variant within the existing prevention and health promotion module
